entries.description: Natural scenes are perceived despite attention being directed to another task and therefore do not produce inattentional blindness.
entries.citation_sentence: It has previously been claimed that inattentional blindness does not occur for natural scenes [17].
entries.notes: Experiment 1a tested this claim using a more demanding multiple-object-tracking task and found substantial inattentional blindness.

entries.original_title: Why does natural scene categorization require little attention? Exploring attentional requirements for natural and synthetic stimuli
entries.original_authors: Fei-Fei, Li; Vanrullen, Rufin; Koch, Christof; Perona, Pietro
entries.description: Natural-scene perception, including detection and categorization of scene contents, is largely unaffected by a demanding concurrent task.
entries.citation_sentence: Given that we followed previous studies in using a task that required the detection and classification of animals and vehicles within a scene, the difference in results between the current study and previous studies [16][29][35] cannot be attributed to a difference in the task used to assess scene perception.
entries.notes: Experiment 3 found dual-task costs for both five-category scene classification and animal-vehicle classification, but the replication used a demanding RSVP task and therefore provides conditional rather than unqualified evidence.

entries.original_title: Speed of processing in the human visual system
entries.original_authors: Thorpe, Simon; Fize, Denis; Marlot, Catherine
entries.description: Animals and other semantic information in natural scenes can be detected and categorized rapidly with minimal attention.
entries.citation_sentence: Given that we followed previous studies in using a task that required the detection and classification of animals and vehicles within a scene, the difference in results between the current study and previous studies [16][29][35] cannot be attributed to a difference in the task used to assess scene perception.
entries.notes: Experiment 3 found dual-task costs for the animal-vehicle scene task when paired with RSVP.
